summary:
Tláloc is an interactive agricultural decision-support platform that transforms NASA Earth observation data into actionable environmental insights for more resilient farming. It features an interactive geospatial workspace where users can explore precipitation, temperature, relative humidity, soil moisture, and elevation through five environmental data layers.

Beyond environmental visualization, Tlaloc incorporates a transparent, rule-based crop rotation assessment engine that evaluates three-year crop sequences. It considers water conservation, soil health restoration, climate resilience, and indicative economic potential, combining NASA-derived environmental indicators with crop characteristics and agronomic criteria to rank alternatives and explain their scores.

By connecting Earth observation data with agricultural decision-making, Tlaloc helps farmers better understand environmental constraints, explore alternative crop rotations, and make more informed long-term planning decisions. Its goal is to support sustainable agriculture, improve resource management, and strengthen farming resilience against changing climate conditions.
details:
🌱 Tlaloc: Agricultural Decision-Support Application

Tlaloc is an agricultural decision-support application designed for smallholder farmers in El Salvador. It integrates NASA Earth observation and climate data with weather forecasts and farmers' own land records to help them better understand their agricultural conditions and make informed farming decisions.

🗺️ Key Features & Crop Rotation Engine

Through an interactive, map-based workspace, users can organize their agricultural plots and explore environmental insights, including:

  • Precipitation & Relative Humidity
  • Temperature
  • Soil Moisture
  • Elevation

Beyond data visualization, Tlaloc incorporates a three-year crop rotation evaluation engine that assesses alternative planting sequences across four key dimensions:

  1. Water Conservation
  2. Soil Health Restoration
  3. Climate Resilience
  4. Indicative Economic Potential

This approach combines NASA-derived environmental indicators with crop characteristics and agronomic criteria to deliver transparent and explainable evaluations.

🎯 Project Objectives & Expected Impact

The project aims to make scientific and environmental information more accessible to farmers, empowering them to explore agricultural strategies tailored to local conditions.

Expected Impact:

  • Promote responsible water management
  • Support soil conservation
  • Enhance climate adaptation
  • Contribute to long-term local food resilience

🛠️ Tech Stack & Architecture

Tlaloc is built as a web application and requires no dedicated hardware:

  • Frontend: TypeScript, Next.js, and React
  • Interactive Mapping & Geospatial Analysis: MapLibre, deck.gl, and Turf.js
  • Backend Services: NestJS
  • Cloud & Infrastructure: AWS (including DynamoDB and S3), managed via AWS CDK

💡 Innovation & Accessibility

Tlaloc's creativity lies in connecting satellite observations, climate data, and agronomic knowledge within a single platform—transforming complex scientific data into practical agricultural insights. Our team carefully considered:

  • The specific needs of smallholder farmers in El Salvador
  • Local environmental conditions
  • Bilingual accessibility in both Spanish and English
  • The integration of scientific, technological, engineering, and business perspectives

🤖 AI Usage Disclosure

We declare the use of AI as a tool to streamline our workflow and increase efficiency, emphasizing that human judgment and creativity are what truly drive our solution:
  • Claude: Software programming and code debugging.
  • Devin: Programming assistance and data analysis.
  • Gemini: Dataset processing and data analysis.
  • ChatGPT: Image generation, video editing assistance, and documentation writing.
  • NanoBanana: Image creation and visual asset design.
  • Google Flow: Video clip generation and image creation.
